entities.title: Rust regex dialect
entities.summary: find's patterns are Rust regular expressions: no look-around and no backreferences.
entities.impact: A pattern that uses them is refused with `invalid regex: ...; rewrite without it or use -F`.
entities.workaround: Rewrite the pattern, or search for literal text with -F.

entities.title: Large and binary files are not searched
entities.summary: find and refs skip files over 2 MiB and files with a NUL byte in their first 8000 bytes, and count them in the footer.
entities.impact: Text in a large generated file, a log or a binary is not found.
entities.workaround: Read the file with read, which accepts files up to 256 MiB.

entities.title: refs matches text, not meaning
entities.summary: refs finds the symbol as a case-sensitive whole word; a match on the first line of an outline symbol of that name is a definition, every other match a use. Only in C# files are matches in comments and strings left out, by tree-sitter.
entities.impact: Outside C#, mentions in comments and strings count as uses; same-named symbols in different scopes are not told apart; files without a grammar get heuristic definitions; and fields, locals and parameters are listed as uses, since only the outline's symbols count as definitions. A C# line with a real use keeps every match on it.

entities.title: read's budget is per file
entities.summary: read applies its token budget to each file it is given, and its output is not cut by the global budget.
entities.impact: One read of many files can return several budgets' worth of text.
entities.workaround: Read files one at a time, or give a smaller --budget.

entities.title: What the atomic replace does not keep
entities.summary: A file with several hard links is rewritten in place rather than replaced; extended attributes are not carried over by the replace.
entities.impact: An edit of a hard-linked file is not atomic; an edited file loses its extended attributes.

entities.title: The terse C# view needs the indexer and a git work tree
entities.summary: A C# file is shown as a terse view only when zazzle-csharp-indexer can be found and started and the file lies inside a git work tree; otherwise read returns the source with a line saying why.
entities.impact: Outside git, or without the indexer installed, C# files cost as many tokens as any other source.

entities.title: The HTML and Razor view works on whole lines
entities.summary: markup.rs does not parse markup: it hides comments and <style>/<svg> elements only when they start and end their own lines, keeps <script>, <pre>, <textarea> and Razor code blocks unchanged, and leaves C# inside Razor code blocks unshortened.
entities.impact: Minified or single-line HTML, and Razor views that are mostly C#, gain little from the view.

entities.title: The Python, TypeScript and Dart view is syntactic
entities.summary: terse.rs works from the syntax tree alone: loggers are recognised by name, nothing is resolved across files, local variables keep their names, and only what stands alone on its lines is hidden.
entities.impact: Logging through a differently named object, or helper wrappers, stays visible, and these views are less compact than the C# view, which also shortens locals.
